question.problem:
Find the smallest natural number solution to the system of linear congruences below.

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x≡4 & (\text{mod}\,7) \\ x≡8 & (\text{mod}\,10)\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Since $7$ and $10$ are coprime, then according to the Chinese remainder theorem, the system has a unique solution modulo $7\cdot 10=70.$

From the first congruence, we get

$$
x≡4\,(\text{mod}\,7)\,⟹\,x=4+7t,\,t\in Z.
$$

Substituting this into the second congruence, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ≡8 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,10) \\ 4+7t & ≡8 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,10) \\ 7t & ≡4 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,10)\end{aligned}
$$

Since $10$ is a relatively small modulus, by trial and error, we have that $3\cdot 7≡1\,(\text{mod}\,10).$ So, we multiply both sides by $3:$

$$
\begin{aligned}7t & ≡4 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,10) \\ 3\cdot 7t & ≡12 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,10) \\ t & ≡2 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,10)\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, $t=2+10s,$ where $s\in Z.$ Substituting this into the expression for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =4+7t \\  & =4+7(2+10s) \\  & =18+70s.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x≡18\,(\text{mod}\,70)$ is the unique solution modulo $70,$ and $x=18$ is the smallest natural number solution to the system.
